question.text: Will the SPARC tokamak announce it has achieved first plasma before 2027?
question.resolution_criteria: This question will resolve as Yes if, before 2027, Commonwealth Fusion Systems officially announces that the SPARC tokamak produced its first plasma.
question.fine_print: This question will resolve based upon official statements from CFS, including their official [press page](https://cfs.energy/news-and-media/) and [blog](https://blog.cfs.energy/).

research:
I found nothing suggesting SPARC will announce first plasma before 2027. CFS has not announced it, every current source targets 2027, and as of the last public counts the machine was still being assembled.

## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-10-27: The CFS press page lists releases through 10.21.2026 (an $85M letter of intent with the Commerce Department). None of them announces first plasma, and the page gives no first-plasma date. [CFS news](https://cfs.energy/news-and-media/)
- 2026-10-27: The newest CFS blog post is dated Oct 22, 2026 (about the $85M federal award). No post announces first plasma. [CFS blog](https://blog.cfs.energy/)
- 2026-08-05: The background post says SPARC is "now almost 80% complete" and that magnet installation is under way. It gives no first-plasma date. [CFS blog](https://blog.cfs.energy/sparc-progress-doe-milestone-approvals-reflect-cfs-power-plant-maturity/)

## 2. Current status
- No first-plasma announcement has been made. About two months remain before the deadline.
- 2026-08-28: CFS wrote "after we start operating SPARC in coming months". It also said "SPARC's first full operations will produce what's called first plasma". There was no date. [CFS blog](https://blog.cfs.energy/why-cfs-is-confident-well-demonstrate-net-fusion-energy-q1/)
- 2026-10-19: A tracker says SPARC is "under construction", with the first-plasma target at 2027 (it slipped from 2025 to 2026 to 2027). The last magnet count it shows is two toroidal-field magnets in Tokamak Hall as of 2026-04-09, out of 18. [Nuclear News Network](https://www.nuclearnewsnetwork.com/industry-trackers/fusion-energy-companies/cfs-sparc)
- One secondary source says all 18 magnets were due by end of summer 2026, but that target slipped, with only three publicly confirmed in late June. The same source says officials target finishing assembly by end of 2027 and first plasma in late 2027. I could not verify this with CFS. [The Fusion Report](https://thefusionreport.com/commonwealth-fusion-systems-a-hot-start-for-2026/)
- Co-founder Brandon Sorbom is quoted as "aiming for first plasma in 2027" when the machine was about 75% built. [Click Petroleo e Gas](https://en.clickpetroleoegas.com.br/commonwealth-fusion-systems-installs-a-48-ton-vessel-and-reaches-75-of-the-sparc-reactor-in-massachusetts-davila/)
- Reported steps still needed before first plasma: closing the cryostat and calibrating neutron diagnostics. The first plasma will use hydrogen only. This is from a secondary search summary, not verified.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-10-22: Blog post on how an $85M federal award would help CFS and the US chip industry. [CFS blog](https://blog.cfs.energy/)
- 2026-10-08: CFS will lead an AI digital-twin fusion project in phase 2 of the Genesis Mission. [CFS news](https://cfs.energy/news-and-media/)
- 2026-09-30: CFS placed its largest single HTS tape order, with Fujikura (reported as for ARC). [CFS news](https://cfs.energy/news-and-media/)
- 2026-09-16: Blog post on cryogenics for SPARC's magnets. One unverified secondary source says the cryogenic plant passed commissioning that day. [CFS blog](https://blog.cfs.energy/)
- 2026-09-10: Hyundai Motor Group made an equity investment. [CFS news](https://cfs.energy/news-and-media/)
- 2026-08: Fusion Energy Base says CFS is targeting "first plasma and scientific breakeven in 2027". [FEB](https://www.fusionenergybase.com/articles/confinement-time-august-2026)
- 2026-07-30: CFS raised $1B more, $4B in total. CEO Mumgaard said SPARC is about 80% complete. [CFS news](https://cfs.energy/news-and-media/)
- 2026-07-08: Blog post "CFS prepares SPARC's fusion support systems for dress rehearsal". [CFS blog](https://blog.cfs.energy/)
- 2026-01-06: The first toroidal-field magnet was installed (CES 2026). TechCrunch said CFS hoped to turn the device on "next year". [TechCrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2026/01/06/commonwealth-fusion-systems-installs-reactor-magnet-lands-deal-with-nvidia/)
- Wikipedia's infobox lists first plasma as 2027 (projected). [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SPARC_(tokamak))

## 4. Base rates
- SPARC's own target has slipped twice: operations in 2025, then first plasma in 2026, then 2027. [NNN](https://www.nuclearnewsnetwork.com/industry-trackers/fusion-energy-companies/cfs-sparc)
- In 2024, MIT News reported first plasma expected in 2026. [MIT News](https://news.mit.edu/2024/commonwealth-fusion-systems-unveils-worlds-first-fusion-power-plant-1217)
- Large tokamaks and stellarators (ITER, JT-60SA, Wendelstein 7-X) have usually reached first plasma later than planned. I did not find any that came in ahead of a target set a year or more earlier. This is general knowledge, not something I sourced for this question.
- The gap from a machine being 75-80% assembled to first plasma has generally been more than a year.

## 5. Other forecasts
- I found no Polymarket, Manifold or Metaculus market on SPARC first plasma.
- Kalshi's "When will nuclear fusion be achieved?" market (Before 2030: 0.30; Before 2035: 0.47; Before 2040: 0.51) is about a different event and does not match this question.
- None of the other markets collected are related.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- Any CFS update on the magnet count or on closing the cryostat. Either would be needed before first plasma.
- Possible year-end progress posts on the CFS blog in December 2026.
- I found no scheduled CFS event before 2027-01-01 that is tied to a first-plasma date.

forecasts.reasoning:
(a) About 2 months remain (now 2026-10-27, deadline 2027-01-01). For Yes, CFS must officially announce, on its press page or blog, that SPARC has produced first plasma before 2027.

(b) If nothing changes, the answer is No. No announcement exists, and every current target is 2027.

(c) Base rate: large tokamaks and stellarators (ITER, JT-60SA, W7-X and SPARC's own history) rarely beat their stated first-plasma schedule. SPARC has already slipped from 2025 to 2026 to 2027. For a machine whose official target is the following year, the chance of first plasma within the current year, with two months left, is under 5%. I put it at about 2-3%.

(d) Evidence:
- For Yes:
  - On 2026-08-28 CFS wrote "after we start operating SPARC in coming months", which is vague but suggests near-term operations.
  - An unverified secondary source says the cryogenic plant passed commissioning on 2026-09-16.
  - The machine was about 80% complete by July/August 2026.
- For No:
  - Only 2-3 of 18 toroidal-field magnets were publicly confirmed installed by April to June 2026.
  - Officials target the end of assembly and first plasma in late 2027.
  - Co-founder Sorbom said they are "aiming for first plasma in 2027".
  - The tracker as of 2026-10-19 still lists 2027 and "under construction".
  - Still to come before first plasma: installing the remaining magnets, closing the cryostat, cooling the HTS magnets and integrated commissioning. Together these take many months.
  - No first-plasma announcement had been made as of 2026-10-27.

(e) Scenarios:
- No: magnet installation and cryostat closure continue into 2027, CFS posts a year-end progress update, and first plasma comes in late 2027.
- Yes: magnet installation went much faster than publicly reported, the cryostat closed in November, cooldown and commissioning go flawlessly, and CFS announces a hydrogen first plasma in late December. This is extremely unlikely given the remaining steps.

(f) I start from a base rate of about 3%. The specific evidence (magnet counts, an official 2027 target, and cooldown and commissioning timelines that cannot fit into 2 months) pushes the estimate lower. I keep a small allowance for unreported progress, such as faster magnet installation than the public counts show. That lands at about 2%.

Probability: 2%

(a) **Time left and what Yes requires.** About 9 weeks remain, from 2026-10-27 to 2027-01-01. Yes requires CFS to officially announce, before 2027, that SPARC has produced its first plasma.

(b) **Status quo.** There is no announcement. SPARC is still being assembled (about 80% complete as of July 2026), and every public target says 2027. If nothing changes, the answer is No.

(c) **Base rate.** The reference class is large fusion devices (ITER, JT-60SA, W7-X, SPARC itself) achieving first plasma ahead of a schedule that was public a year or more earlier, or reaching first plasma within about 2 months of being roughly 80% assembled. I found no such cases. SPARC's own target has slipped twice. I put the base rate at about 1-3%.

(d) **Strongest evidence.**
- For Yes: on 2026-08-28 the CFS blog said "after we start operating SPARC in coming months." The cryogenic plant reportedly passed commissioning on 2026-09-16 (unverified). On 2026-07-08 there was a "dress rehearsal" post about support systems.
- For No:
  - Only 2-3 of 18 toroidal-field magnets were publicly confirmed installed by April to June 2026, and the end-of-summer target for all 18 slipped.
  - Officials reportedly target finishing assembly by end of 2027, with first plasma in late 2027.
  - Sorbom, Fusion Energy Base (August 2026) and Wikipedia all say 2027.
  - The cryostat still has to be closed, and the high-temperature superconducting magnets need a multi-week cooldown before any plasma.
  - CFS press releases through 2026-10-21 show nothing close to a first-plasma event.

(e) **Scenarios.**
- No: magnet installation and integration continue through 2026, and CFS posts a year-end progress update while first plasma stays targeted for 2027. This is very likely.
- Yes: the magnet installation went far faster than publicly reported and the cryostat is closed by November. CFS then rushes a low-field or hydrogen "first plasma" shot in late December for a PR milestone. This is highly implausible given the assembly state.

(f) **From base rate to final number.** I start near 2%. The "coming months" phrasing adds a sliver of uncertainty, but the magnet count and the remaining assembly and cooldown steps make a 2026 first plasma physically very unlikely. I hold at about 2%. I don't go lower because the latest magnet count is unknown and the "coming months" wording leaves some tail.

Probability: 2%

(a) About 2 months remain, from 2026-10-27 to 2027-01-01. For Yes, CFS must officially announce, on its press page or blog, that SPARC produced its first plasma before 2027.

(b) Status quo: no announcement. SPARC was still being assembled as of the latest public reports, so if nothing changed the answer would be No.

(c) Base rate: large tokamaks and stellarators (ITER, JT-60SA, W7-X, KSTAR, EAST) almost never reach first plasma earlier than a target set a year or more before. CFS's public target is 2027 and has already slipped twice. For a machine reported as about 80% complete with first plasma due the next year, the chance of hitting it within 2 months is about 1-3%.

(d) Evidence:
- For Yes:
  - 2026-08-28: a CFS blog post said "after we start operating SPARC in coming months."
  - 2026-07-30: CFS said SPARC was about 80% complete.
  - 2026-09-16: cryogenic plant commissioning was reported, though not verified.
- For No:
  - Every source targets 2027, including Sorbom's "aiming for first plasma in 2027" and Fusion Energy Base in August 2026. The Fusion Report says late 2027.
  - Public reports confirmed only 2-3 of the 18 toroidal-field magnets installed by April-June 2026.
  - Before first plasma, CFS still has to install the central solenoid and poloidal-field coils, close the cryostat, cool down the magnets over several weeks and commission the systems.
  - CFS press and blog posts through Oct 22 contain no first-plasma news.

(e) Scenarios:
- No: magnet installation and integration continue through year-end, with a commissioning update in December and first plasma in 2027.
- Yes: the remaining magnets went in quickly and quietly, the cryostat closed in October, and a fast cooldown leads to a hydrogen first plasma announced in late December. This is highly implausible given the steps still to come.

(f) I start from a base rate of about 2%. The "coming months" wording keeps a sliver of hope, but the remaining assembly and cooldown sequence makes a 2026 first plasma physically very unlikely. I stay at about 2%.

Probability: 2%

(a) About 2 months remain, until 2027-01-01. For Yes, CFS must officially announce, on its press page or blog, that SPARC produced its first plasma before the end of 2026.

(b) Status quo: No. SPARC is still being assembled. Toroidal-field magnet installation was well short of 18 as of mid-2026, and no first-plasma announcement exists.

(c) Base rate: large fusion devices almost never reach first plasma ahead of a target set a year or more earlier. Examples include ITER, JT-60SA and W7-X. SPARC's own date has slipped from 2025 to 2026 to 2027. For a machine about 80% assembled whose official target is the following year, the chance of first plasma within the next 2 months is roughly 1-3%.

(d) Evidence:
- For Yes:
  - 2026-08-28: the CFS blog spoke of "after we start operating SPARC in coming months."
  - 2026-09-16: the cryogenic plant was reportedly commissioned.
  - 2026-07-08: CFS described a support-systems "dress rehearsal."
- For No:
  - Every current source targets first plasma in 2027 (Sorbom; Fusion Energy Base, August 2026; Wikipedia; NNN as of 2026-10-19).
  - Only about 3 of 18 TF magnets were publicly confirmed installed by late June 2026.
  - The cryostat is not closed.
  - Magnet cooldown and integrated commissioning take months after assembly.
  - Recent CFS news (October 2026) is about funding and HTS orders, not imminent operation.
  - One secondary source says officials target late 2027.

(e) No scenario: magnet installation continues through late 2026, the cryostat closes in 2027, and after cooldown and commissioning first plasma happens in the second half of 2027. This is the most likely path.
Yes scenario: magnet installation went much faster than publicly reported, and the cryostat closed in the fall. CFS then does a rushed cooldown, gets a symbolic hydrogen first plasma in late December, and announces it before year end. This is very unlikely given the physical sequence still required.

(f) I start at about 2% and keep it there. The "coming months" phrasing nudges me up slightly. The magnet count, the remaining physical steps and the consistent 2027 targets keep me low. I also leave a small allowance for things that were not publicly reported.

Probability: 2%

**(a) Time left and what Yes requires:** About 2 months remain, until 2027-01-01. For Yes, CFS must officially announce, on its press page or blog, that SPARC has produced first plasma before that date.

**(b) Status quo:** No announcement has been made. SPARC is still being assembled. Every current CFS-linked and secondary source targets 2027. If nothing changes, the answer is No.

**(c) Base rate:** Large fusion devices such as ITER, JT-60SA and W7-X have nearly always reached first plasma later than planned. None that I know of beat a target set a year or more earlier. The gap from roughly 80% assembled to first plasma has generally been over a year. For a device that is 80% complete and targeting next year, the base rate for first plasma within 2 months is about 1-2%.

**(d) Evidence:**
- **For Yes:**
  - On 2026-08-28, CFS wrote "after we start operating SPARC in coming months."
  - The cryogenics work was publicized on 2026-09-16, and one unverified source says the cryogenic plant passed commissioning that day.
  - A "dress rehearsal" post for the support systems appeared on 2026-07-08.
- **For No:**
  - Only 2-3 of 18 toroidal-field magnets were publicly confirmed installed as of April-June 2026.
  - The end-of-summer target for all magnets slipped.
  - Officials reportedly target finishing assembly by end of 2027, with first plasma in late 2027.
  - Sorbom said CFS is aiming for first plasma in 2027.
  - Fusion Energy Base (August 2026) says CFS is targeting first plasma in 2027.
  - TechCrunch (January 2026) reported CFS hoped to turn the device on "next year."
  - The project already has a history of slipping its schedule.

**(e) Scenarios:**
- **No:** Magnet installation, cryostat closure, pump-down and magnet cooldown continue through 2026. First plasma comes in mid-to-late 2027 or later.
- **Yes:** Assembly turns out to be far further along than the public counts show. CFS has quietly finished all the magnets, closes the cryostat, cools down quickly, and fires a hydrogen plasma in December to announce it as a year-end milestone. This is implausible given that cooldown alone for large superconducting magnets takes weeks to months.

**(f) Adjustment:** I start at about 1-2%. The phrase "coming months" and the cryogenics progress justify a very slight upward nudge for uncertainty about how far along assembly really is. However, the hard physical sequence still remaining (magnets, cryostat, vacuum, cooldown, integrated commissioning) makes an announcement before 2027 essentially infeasible. I settle at about 2%.

Probability: 2%
